summary: Reference for the IK Retargeter asset and Retarget Editor: creating the retargeter from IK Rigs, defining retarget chains and the pelvis, editing/importing retarget poses (A-pose vs T-pose, Auto Align), the op stack, exporting retargeted Animation Sequences, and Override Sets/Variables driven at runtime via the Retarget Pose From Mesh node.
gotchas: Both source and target need IK Rig assets with matching retarget chains and a pelvis defined
Chain names are matched by fuzzy string match, so keep names consistent
Retarget variables cannot be arrays, maps, or sets; an override set must be active for bound variables to apply
Override Sets replace the former Retarget Profiles workflow; use an existing (not auto-generated) retargeter for batch export with overrides

summary: Explains the legacy Retarget Manager in the Skeleton Editor: adding retarget sources so mesh-specific animations keep proportions, assigning a Humanoid Rig with bone-to-node mapping for cross-skeleton retargeting, and setting a Retargeted Base Pose (including from a Pose Asset).
gotchas: Mismatched base poses (A-pose vs T-pose) cause wrong arm positions unless a Retargeted Base Pose is set
Non-biped characters need a custom Rig asset instead of Humanoid

summary: How to auto-generate and tune Skeletal Mesh LODs with the Skeletal Mesh Reduction Tool: Number of LODs, Bones to Prioritize, Lock Mesh Edges, Termination Criterion, Volumetric Correction, removing bones per LOD, plus a property reference and LOD console commands.
gotchas: Requires Skeletal Mesh Reduction Plugin set to SkeletalMeshReduction in Project Settings
Regenerating a LOD overwrites any existing LOD, including ones imported from a DCC
Generation can take time depending on mesh complexity and hardware

summary: Covers the in-editor Skeleton Editing tools: converting a Static Mesh to a Skeletal Mesh, adding/orienting/mirroring/renaming bones, binding and painting skin weights (brush and vertex modes), attribute maps, hotkeys, and Python automation via SkeletonModifier and SkinWeightModifier.
gotchas: Requires the Skeletal Mesh Editing Tools plugin and an editor restart
Skin weights are auto-normalized to 1; a single-influence vertex cannot be reduced below 1.0
Prefer adding weight to other bones rather than removing weight
Flooding a bone's weights to 0 sends them back to the root bone

summary: Explains Virtual Bones (bones that follow a target bone but live under another parent) and a worked Anim Blueprint setup using Slots, Apply Additive, a Blend Mask in Layered Blend per Bone, and Two Bone IK to stop hand/foot swimming during additive animations.
gotchas: Virtual bones must be excluded from the additive layer via a Blend Mask with blend value 0.0
Joint Target Location (pole vector) depends on the character; mannequin uses X -25, Y -50, Z 0

summary: UI reference for the Sound Cue Editor: menu bar entries, toolbar buttons (Play Cue, Play Node, Solo, Mute, Stop), and the Details, Viewport (Sound Node Graph) and Palette panels.
gotchas: Play Node is only available while a single node is selected

summary: Node-by-node reference for Sound Cues: the Output node (sound class, attenuation, submix, concurrency, priority) and Attenuation, Branch, Concatenator, Continuous Modulator, Crossfade, Delay, Doppler, Enveloper, Looping, Mixer, Modulator, Oscillator, Random, Switch, Wave Param and Wave Player nodes, plus how named parameters are set from Blueprint.
gotchas: Named parameters cannot be set inside the Sound Cue; the In Name in the Blueprint/code call must match exactly
The Looping node is not seamless; use the Looping flag on Wave Player for seamless loops
Sound Cues without an Attenuation node are not localized
Crossfade by Param does not support negative values; Random Preselect at Level Load does not apply in PIE

summary: How to create, edit, copy and convert Sockets in the Skeleton Tree (including mesh-only Mesh Sockets) and attach actors to them in the level, in Blueprint components via Parent Socket, or dynamically with Attach/Detach functions and their transform rules.
gotchas: Sockets edit the Skeleton asset (Mesh Sockets edit the Skeletal Mesh), so that asset must be saved
Sockets are hidden in the viewport by default (Character > Bones > Sockets)
Level attachment keeps the object's world transform; zero its transform to match the socket

summary: Hub page for Datasmith workflow tutorials; contains no content beyond a pointer to the tutorial list.

Overview of the shared Animation Editor window: toolbar (Preview Mesh, Preview Animation, Create Asset menu for sequences, montages, blend spaces, aim offsets, Anim Blueprints), viewport stats, the five editor modes, and Preview Scene Settings.

Step-by-step guide to creating Behavior Tree and Blackboard assets, custom Blueprint Tasks, Decorators and Services, adding Blackboard keys, assigning the Blackboard to the tree, and wiring/editing nodes in the Behavior Tree Editor.
gotchas: Only Composite nodes can connect to the Root node
Connections only go output to input
For performance consider native (C++) Tasks/Services instead of Blueprint ones
Rename auto-named Task/Decorator/Service assets created from the toolbar

summary: Describes Font assets (Runtime composite vs Offline atlas caching), Font Face assets with Hinting, Loading Policy and Layout Method settings, and the Font Editor including Default and Sub-Font Families for per-character-range fonts such as Japanese.
gotchas: Update/Export toolbar options only work in Offline cache mode
Stream loading can cause hitches; Inline is hitch-free but uses more memory
Try Bounding Box layout if a font clips or has wrong line height

summary: Conceptual page on Niagara's design: modules (graph/HLSL), emitters and systems (stacks), stack groups and Spawn/Update/Event/Simulation stages, and which namespaces each group can read or write.
gotchas: Simulation Stages are an advanced GPU feature
Particle-group modules can only read from System and Emitter namespaces, not write them

summary: Interface reference for the Media Editor opened from a Media Player asset: playback toolbar, player window and capture devices, track/format playback options, Media Library, Playlist, Details (Play on Open, Loop, Shuffle) and the Info panel for debugging video playback.
gotchas: Looping Video Capture devices is not supported
Unsupported formats show as Not supported in the Info panel

summary: Reference for the nDisplay 3D Config Editor used to define multi-display clusters: screen/mesh/Xform/View Origin/ICVFX camera components, cluster nodes and hosts, output mapping and remapping, viewports, projection policies and TextureShare.
gotchas: Output Remapping with a Static Mesh requires Allow CPUAccess on the mesh
Rotating output with an external file requires manually resizing the application window

summary: Overview of Niagara systems, emitters (Emitter/Particle Spawn and Update, Event Handler, Render groups), modules, parameter types, the Niagara Asset Browser and custom Asset Tag Definitions, plus inheritance, dynamic inputs, micro expressions, events and data interfaces.
gotchas: Some template systems need the Niagara Fluids plugin enabled
Each module, emitter and system costs resources; prefer existing modules and dynamic inputs over new modules

summary: Short landing page for the Physics Asset Editor: what Physics Assets are (bodies and constraints for Skeletal Mesh ragdolls/collision), how to create them on import or from the Content Drawer, and how to open the editor; links to Physics Bodies, Constraints and tutorials.
gotchas: Only a single Physics Asset is used per Skeletal Mesh

summary: Explains Skeleton assets: creation on FBX import or via Create Skeleton, Skeleton Tree icons, the animation data stored on the skeleton (notifies, curves, slots, blend masks), rules for sharing one skeleton across meshes, merging on import, and Compatible Skeletons via the Retarget Manager.
gotchas: Sharing a skeleton requires identical bone names and hierarchy order; extra bones may only be appended
Inserting bones can cause transform offsets
Compatible skeletons are bi-directional and need near-identical hierarchies and proportions

summary: Introduces Sound Waves and Sound Cues, how to create a Sound Cue, open the editor, add nodes to the Sound Node Graph and preview playback.
gotchas: Sound Wave property changes affect every Sound Cue that references it
Build graphs left to right ending at the Output node

summary: Basics of Static Mesh Actors: placing them by drag-and-drop, overriding materials per actor, setting Mobility to Movable to move them at runtime, enabling Simulate Physics, and default collision behavior.
gotchas: Static Mesh Actors default to Static mobility and must be set to Movable to move during play
Collision only exists if the mesh has physics bodies

summary: UI reference for the Static Mesh Editor: menus (including simplified collision generation like box/sphere/capsule/k-DOP and Auto Convex), toolbar (reimport, UV display), viewport stats, view modes, show flags, LOD selection, Details panel, bottom toolbar and controls.
keys: Copy Collision from Selected Static Mesh
gotchas: Unique non-overlapping UVs are required for shadow mapping
Realtime viewport is off by default, so streamed textures may need a click to load at full resolution

summary: Tutorial building a HUD with UMG in the First Person template: creating Widget Blueprints, Create Widget plus Add to Viewport from the character, laying out Horizontal/Vertical Boxes, Text and Progress Bars, anchors, and property bindings for health, energy and ammo.
gotchas: Default UMG font supports only a small set of languages; import custom fonts for others
Compile the Blueprint before setting variable default values

summary: Entry page for the Material Editor: steps to create and apply a Material, Live Update options (Preview Material, Realtime Nodes, All Node Previews), compiler error display, and searching the material graph including the NAME= switch.
gotchas: All Node Previews recompiles every node and can be slow on large graphs; disable it and press Spacebar to refresh
Missing or wrongly typed required inputs cause compile errors shown on the node and in Stats

summary: Overview of Sequencer's Level Sequence Asset and Level Sequence Actor, the actor's playback and cinematic settings (Auto Play, Loop, Hide Player, Disable Movement Input), ways to create and bind a Level Sequence, and how to open the Sequencer editor.
gotchas: Opening a sequence from the Content Browser leaves contents unbound unless a level referencing it is open
A sequence only appears in the Cinematics dropdown if assigned to a Level Sequence Actor in the level

summary: Hub page for the Blueprint Editor UI, linking to interface breakdowns for Level Blueprints, Blueprint Classes, Blueprint Interfaces, Macro Libraries and the Animation Blueprint Editor.
